title: SDK-driven model flipplay cheat sheet
content:
Purpose
Quick personal reference for doing an SDK-driven model flip (what I call a 'flipplay') when we need to move traffic between model variants quickly, with minimal infra ops. This is deliberately operator-facing (notes to self), not the official runbook yet.

Context / when to use
- Use when a small controlled cohort needs to switch from model-A:v1 -> model-A:v2 via client-side SDK routing, to avoid server-side global pins or immediate infra deploys.
- Good for experiments where per-client sticky routing matters (mobile cohorts, internal beta keys).
- Not for large-scale emergency rollbacks (where we should use global alias swap and infra fallback).

High-level flow
1) Preflight checks (local + infra)
   - Confirm v2 is live in target region and proxy accepts alias "model-a:v2-canary" (curl health endpoint).
   - Verify model serving metrics: p50/p95 latency, mem usage, active streams <= expected.
   - Check kv-cache warming status if applicable (redis/kv cache hit rate).
   - Log decisions in GitHub PR (link above) and add RED ticket.
2) SDK feature flag toggle to cohort (0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%)
   - Toggle percent via SDK control plane (see SDK snippet below).
   - Wait at least 10-30 minutes at each step, check telemetry, error budget, and human + automated alerts.
3) Stabilize and expand or roll back
   - If anomalies, flip back to previous alias for affected cohort via SDK or issue global alias unpin.
   - After 100% and 24h stable, create permanent alias pin and update client default.

Operator checklist (quick)
- [ ] Announce to #releases and #oncall 10m before flip
- [ ] Confirm canary infra health + scaling headroom
- [ ] Create ephemeral traffic tag in Telemetry (e.g., flipplay-2025-02-11-AK)
- [ ] Kick off 1% cohort via SDK feature flag
- [ ] Watch these dashboards: tokens/sec, p50/p95 token lat, model error rate, inference queue depth, cost-per-token delta
- [ ] After 2 stable increments, update PR with telemetry snippets and mark experiment as "safe" or "rollback"

SDK snippet (pseudo)
// client-side routing config (JS SDK)
const FlipPlay = {
  name: 'model-a-flipplay',
  cohortPercent: 5, // % of keys that should be routed to v2
  stickyKeyHeader: 'x-client-id',
  alias: 'model-a:v2-canary'
}
redwood.sdk.setRouting(FlipPlay)
// toggle via control-plane API:
// POST /control/flipplay { name: 'model-a-flipplay', percent: 20 }

Telemetry signals to watch (threshold suggestions)
- Increased 5xx inference errors > 0.5% above baseline -> pause expansion
- p95 latency increase > 2x baseline OR absolute > 1200ms -> investigate
- Token cost delta > 30% for same prompt distribution -> notify cost-eng
- Semantic regression: manual sample set scoring drop > 3% absolute -> immediate rollback
- Garbage/poison responses flagged by monitoring -> rollback and attach sample to ticket

Edge cases / gotchas
- Sticky sessions: if clients cache routing decisions longer than expected, a flip can take hours to fully propagate. Use SDK TTL headers to control stickiness.
- SDK offline clients: mobile apps with older SDKs may ignore the new flag; have a fallback server-side alias swap option ready.
- Mixed-region traffic: ensure alias v2 is deployed in all regions serving that cohort or SDK will silently route to fallback.

Rollback play (fast)
- Step 0: Stop expansion and set cohortPercent to 0 (SDK) for the flipplay name.
- Step 1: If client-side toggle insufficient, issue global alias unpin: POST /models/aliases/unpin { alias: 'model-a:prod' } -> revert to model-a:v1
- Step 2: Re-run quick QA suite (smoke prompts) against v1 and v2 side-by-side, attach failing prompts to RED ticket.
- Step 3: If underlying infra is root cause, escalate to s-re team (pager duty).

Postmortem notes (template to copy after event)
- Timeline of toggles + hours
- Telemetry deltas at each percent step
- Root cause and fix (model change vs infra vs client SDK bug)
- Owner for follow-up: (e.g., QA regression test addition, SDK TTL change, deployment checklist update)

Unresolved questions / TODOs (personal)
- Decide on default cohort step time (10m vs 30m). I lean 20m for heavy models. Need experiment data.
- Add automatic sniffing in control plane to suggest rollback if p95 spikes rapidly. Ticket RED-8420 assigned.
- Formalize SDK TTL semantics across mobile/web to prevent sticky linger.

Notes to self
- Keep flipplay names short and timestamped. Follow pattern: flipplay-MMDD-initiator (flipplay-0211-ak).
- Avoid flipplay for paid enterprise customers that expect global deterministic aliasing unless buyer consented.
- When in doubt, do global alias swap during quiet window (US early morning) instead of client-side flip.

Useful links / commands
- Health check: curl -H 'Host: model-a' https://model-serving.region.redwood/health
- Control plane toggle: curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://control.redwood/api/flipplay -d '{"name":"model-a-flipplay","percent":5}'
- PR with last flip experiment: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1324

Last tested: 2025-02-25 (small internal beta, mobile cohort, 10% budget). Observations: slight p95 increase (~12%), no user-facing errors, client SDK stickiness ~18min median.

End of scratchpad — convert to proper playbook once we validate TTL and automation thresholds.
